ai_summary.headline: Syria asks for USD 183m of MPC, 6.3% of the plan, and is 20% funded against it.
ai_summary.narrative: The 2026 HNRP targets 8.6 million people and requests USD 2.92bn; MPC is USD 183.4m, about 6.3%, up 26% on 2025 [s2][s3][s4]. MPCA aims to reach 1.6 million people, with provisional transfer values of USD 100 a month for regular and USD 150 for emergency assistance, pending an updated S/MEB [s4]. By late October the plan was 33% funded; MPC had received USD 36.6m, 20% of its requirement on FTS's single-cluster view (USD 71.1m, 39%, counting shared-cluster flows), so cash is funded worse than the plan average [s1][s2]. The HNRP reports cash as the top priority for 85% of households surveyed, though only 27% received any aid and food made up 64% of support [s5]. A CWG coordinates MPCA with deduplication in place [s4], and CashCap co-authored a 2025 feasibility analysis [s6]. Cost-efficiency, pooled-fund cash shares and CWG leadership were not found. The gap between stated priority and delivery appears to be the strongest advocacy angle, but that is inference.
barriers: Plan 33% funded; coverage only 27% of households
Transfer values provisional until S/MEB is endorsed
Market monitoring products not clearly recurring in 2026
No cost-efficiency or pooled-fund cash data found
opportunities: Cash cited as top household priority (85%), well above its share of requirements
Feasibility analysis and CWG deduplication system provide a base for scale-up

ctp_usd.note: All flows tagged 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)', inside or outside the MPC cluster.

sectoral_cva_usd.note: Flows whose FTS modality field is 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)' and whose destination cluster is not multi-purpose cash: 87 flows. The CTP tag is set by the reporting donor or agency and is not applied consistently, so this is a floor, not a measure of sectoral cash. Largest: Food Security US$11.4M, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene US$6.6M, Shelter US$6.6M.

cva_usd.note: Union of the MPC cluster and the CTP tag. Widest defensible FTS cash figure; still a floor because untagged sectoral cash is invisible.

fts_cva.caveat: FTS records funding, not transfers to people, and only to first-level recipients. Sectoral cash depends on a modality tag that reporters apply unevenly.
